images.title: A building above and below ground
images.purpose: Show that a building has floors on both sides of the ground line, which raises the question of a number below zero.
images.composition: One tall building centred, with a thick grey ground line across its middle and generous white space on both sides.
images.exact_structure: One plain tall building drawn as a stack of 6 equal floor rows, all the same width. A thick grey #6B7280 ground line crosses the building, with 3 floor rows above it filled teal #0072B2 and 3 floor rows below it filled amber #E69F00. No floor numbers and no signs anywhere. Exactly 1 building, 6 floors, 1 ground line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any extra floor, dot, arrow or row beyond the counts stated
unequal floor rows or unequal arrow lengths
images.takeaway: Some floors lie above the ground and some lie below it.
images.description: A plain building of 6 equal floors split by a thick grey ground line: 3 teal floors above and 3 amber floors below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the floors above the ground and then the floors below it, and wonder what to call them.

image_decisions.why: The chapter opener is a simple picture of floors on both sides of the ground; one clean image carries it.
